rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators object that the prayer seems unanswered because Quraysh, among Abraham’s descendants, worshipped idols.
rows.anchor: استشكلوا أولا قوله عليه السلام { واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام } من حيث إن ظاهره سؤال الحفظ

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: They also ask why the Qur’an would quote an unfulfilled prayer as purposeless speech without stating its rejection, unlike its usual practice.
rows.anchor: وهو لغو غير معنى به ثم لا يذكر رده

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: A further objection is that an infallible prophet should not ask to be protected from idol worship.
rows.anchor: ثم كيف يمكن أن يسأل لنفسه المصونية والعصمة عن عبادة الأصنام وهو نبي والأنبياء معصومون

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: One answer takes “my sons” as immediate sons such as Ishmael and Isaac, for whom the prayer was answered.
rows.anchor: قيل في الجواب عن إشكال عدم استجابة دعائه في بنيه أن المراد ببنيه أبناؤه بلا واسطة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Another answer restricts “my sons” to descendants alive when Abraham prayed, who were monotheists.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد الموجودون من بنيه وقت الدعاء وهم موحدون

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A third answer says God answered the prayer for some descendants but not all, without any deficiency in that outcome.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن الله قد استجاب دعاءه في بعض بنيه دون بعض ولا نقص فيه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some say Abraham’s polytheist descendants treated idols as intercessors rather than worshipping them.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن المشركين من بنيه لم يكونوا يعبدون الأصنام وإنما كانوا يتخذونها شفعاء

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Another distinction says they worshipped unfigured idols (awthān), not figured statues (aṣnām).
rows.anchor: وقيل إنهم كانوا يعبدون الأوثان دون الأصنام وبينهما فرق فإن الأصنام هي التماثيل المصورة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A further account says each person set up a stone, called it like the Kaaba, circled it, and named this practice al-dawwār.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنهم ما كانوا يعبدون الأصنام بل كان الواحد منهم ينصب حجرا ويقول هذا حجر والبيت حجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the first two answers as contrary to the wording, the partial-answer explanation as missing the real objection, and the remaining distinctions because all involve worshipful association.
rows.anchor: وسقوط هذه الوجوه ظاهرة أما الأول والثاني فلكونهما خلاف ظاهر اللفظ وأما الثالث فلأن الإشكال ليس في ورود نقص

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: One answer reads the request as asking for continued, lasting protection from idolatry.
rows.anchor: وقيل في الجواب عن إشكال سؤال النبي الإبعاد والإجناب عن الشرك وهو نبي معصوم أن المراد الثبات والدوام على ذلك

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Another answer sees Abraham as humbling himself and displaying his dependence on divine grace.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه عليه السلام ذكر ذلك هضما لنفسه وإظهارا للحاجة إلى فضله تعالى

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A third answer takes the request as protection from hidden association, since prophets are protected from manifest association.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد سؤال الحفظ عن الشرك الخفي وإلا فالأنبياء مصونون عن الشرك الجلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the permanence answer: if infallibility is necessary from the start, it remains necessary, so asking for its continuance is no less problematic.
rows.anchor: أما الأول فلأنه لا ينحسم به مادة الإشكال إذ العصمة والمصونية كما أنها لازمة للنبوة حدوثا لازمة لها بقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine bestowal does not make its recipient independent: need persists, God’s ownership and power remain, and asking expresses need rather than prior deprivation.
rows.anchor: فإن الحاجة من جانب المستفيض باقية على حالها قبل الإفاضة لا تختلف أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Self-abasement applies to nonessential matters, not necessary infallibility; denying essential human status would merely deny perfection, and the proposed display of need also fails on their premise.
rows.anchor: هضم النفس إنما يستقيم في غير الضروريات وأما الأمور الضرورية فلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the hidden-association answer: Abraham explains the request by saying idols led many astray, so he asks protection from manifest idolatry, not inward reliance on other than God.
rows.anchor: فهو إنما يسأل الإبعاد من عبادة هذه الأصنام وهي الشرك الجلي دون الحفظ عن الركون والتوجه إلى غير الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Equating idols with everything one turns toward besides God, and worship with any such orientation, is an unsupported reinterpretation.
rows.anchor: وهو دعوى لا دليل عليها

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators object that Abraham’s words appear to request forgiveness for polytheists, although scripture says God does not forgive association with Him.
rows.anchor: ثم استشكلوا في قوله عليه السلام { ومن عصاني فإنك غفور رحيم } من حيث اشتماله على طلب المغفرة للمشركين

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: One answer says polytheism could be forgiven under earlier dispensations, and only this dispensation prohibited such forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل في الجواب عن الإشكال أن الشرك كان جائز المغفرة في الشرائع السابقة وإنما رفع ذلك في هذه الشريعة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Another answer supplies an unspoken condition: God is forgiving to the one who disobeys Abraham after that person repents.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن المراد ومن عصاني فإنك غفور رحيم له بعد توبته ففي الكلام قيد محذوف

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A third answer reads the request as asking God to forgive and show mercy by bringing a persistently idolatrous disobedient person into monotheism.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد ومن عصاني وأقام على الشرك فإنك غفور رحيم بأن تنقله من الشرك إلى التوحيد

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A fourth answer takes forgiveness as concealing the idolatry in this world and mercy as delaying immediate punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالمغفرة والرحمة الستر على الشرك في الدنيا والرحمة بعدم معاجلة العقاب

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A fifth answer keeps the wording literal and says Abraham spoke before learning that God would not forgive association; such knowledge could come later.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن الكلام على ظاهره وكان ذلك منه عليه السلام قبل أن يعلم أن الله لا يغفر الشرك

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A sixth answer limits the disobedience here to sins short of polytheism.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالمعصية ما دون الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier-law explanation lacks evidence and is contradicted by warnings to Adam’s community and Jesus’ dispensation; Qur’anic judgment, afterlife, intercession, and prophetic prayers show no rescue from shirk except repentance before death.
rows.anchor: دعوى كون الشرك جائز المغفرة في الشرائع السابقة دعوى لا دليل عليها بل الدليل على خلافها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding repentance without a textual qualifier is unwarranted and breaks the contrast: a repentant disobedient person rejoins Abraham’s followers, leaving the comparison one-sided.
rows.anchor: تقييد المغفرة والرحمة بالتوبة تقييد من غير مقيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conversion and worldly-concealment readings depart from the apparent request: forgiveness is sought while disobedience persists and normally removes sin’s consequences, especially in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ظاهر طلب المغفرة للعاصي أن يغفر الله له حينما هو عاص لا أن يغفر الله له بعد خروجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls the ignorance explanation especially implausible: late in life Abraham could not have been ignorant of basic doctrine, interceded without permission, and had God quote uncorrected nonsense; God explicitly justified his earlier prayer for his father by a prior promise.
rows.anchor: أن يجهل ما هو من واضحات المعارف الدينية ثم يجري على جهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Restricting disobedience to lesser sins has no textual qualifier, unless reconstructed along lines already explained.
rows.anchor: تقييد المعصية بما دون الشرك تقييد من غير مقيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exegetes’ difficulties stem from neglecting what divine protection from shirk means and how the follower-belongs-to-me clause follows from the preceding prayer.
rows.anchor: وقد وقعوا فيما وقعوا لإهمالهم تحقيق القول في معنى حفظه تعالى عن الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “I settled some of my descendants,” min is partitive, while the phrase functions as the object of “settled” or stands in its place.
rows.anchor: في تأويل مفعول " أسكنت " أو ساد مسده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descendants meant are Ishmael and the children to be born to him, not Ishmael alone, as the following plural purpose clause indicates.
rows.anchor: ابنه إسماعيل ومن سيولد له من الأولاد دون اسماعيل وحده بدليل قوله بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’anic account of Abraham’s earlier forgiveness prayer for his father says it was only because of a promise; when he learned the man was God’s enemy, he disavowed him.
rows.anchor: وما كان استغفار إبراهيم لأبيه إلا عن موعدة وعدها إياه فلما تبين له أنه عدو لله تبرأ منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Not of cultivation” means uncultivated in a stronger sense: rocky, sandy land lacking the materials needed for crops; he compares the wording with “a Qur’an without crookedness.”
rows.anchor: غير المزروع وهو آكد وأبلغ لأنه يدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The House is attributed to God because it was built for a purpose belonging exclusively to Him: worship; its being sacred is a status God legislated.
rows.anchor: ونسبة البيت إلى الله سبحانه لأنه مبني لغرض لا يصلح إلا له تعالى وهو عبادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “at Your sacred House” syntactically modifies “I settled.”
rows.anchor: والظرف أعني قوله { عند بيتك المحرم } متعلق بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer’s mention of the House and settlement there shows Abraham made this supplication late in life, after building the Kaaba and populating Mecca; the verse about sons born in old age also supports this chronology.
rows.anchor: من الشاهد على ما قدمناه من أنه عليه السلام إنما دعا بهذا الدعاء في أواخر عمره بعد ما بنى الكعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This timing removes the objection that Abraham called it a House before building it; proposals that he foresaw its future construction or that a prior House was destroyed or lifted away are unnecessary and fail to explain other wording on the same chronology.
rows.anchor: ولا حاجة إلى دفعه بأنه كان يعلم بما علمه الله أنه سيبني هناك بيتا لله أو بأن البيت كان قبل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham chose a barren, isolated valley without life’s comforts so his family would devote themselves to worship without worldly distractions.
rows.anchor: يفيد أنه عليه السلام إنما اختار واديا غير ذي زرع أعزل من أمتعة الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hearts’ “falling” toward them means affection and inclination, through living near them or making pilgrimage to the House, so the family can find companionship.
rows.anchor: من الهوي بمعنى السقوط أي تحن وتميل إليهم بالمساكنة معهم أو بالحج إلى البيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provides fruits by bringing them to the valley through trade.
rows.anchor: بالنقل إليهم تجارة { لعلهم يشكرون }

words: ربنا إنك تعلم ما نخفي وما نعلن
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meaning of Abraham’s statement that God knows what they conceal and disclose is plain.
rows.anchor: إلى آخر الآية معناه ظاهر

words: وما يخفى على الله من شيء في الأرض ولا في السماء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about nothing being hidden may continue Abraham’s speech or be God’s own comment; on the first reading, addressing God by name explains why He knows what is hidden and disclosed.
rows.anchor: من تمام كلام إبراهيم عليه السلام أو من كلامه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He suggests “heaven” may mean what is hidden from human perception, while “earth” means what is perceptible to us.
rows.anchor: المراد بالسماء ما هو خفي علينا غائب عن حسنا

words: الحمد لله الذي وهب لي على الكبر إسماعيل وإسحاق
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The praise in 14:39 is an interpolated sentence between parts of the prayer, recalling God’s great gift of two righteous sons in old age after ordinary means of offspring had ceased.
rows.anchor: كالجملة المعترضة بين فقرات دعائه دعاه إلى إيراده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham praises God because He granted the sons in response to his prayer for children.
rows.anchor: وهبهما له باستجابة دعائه للولد فحمد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing prayer is attributable to God through permission and will, and to the servant through undertaking and action, as with asking God to keep one from idolatry.
rows.anchor: لإقامة الصلاة نسبة إليه تعالى بالإذن والمشية كما أن لها نسبة إلى العبد بالتصدي والعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is Abraham’s second prayer shared with descendants; it follows the first shared request to be kept and his sons from idol worship, and is followed by a third shared prayer for forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وهذه الفقرة ثاني دعاء يشترك فيه هو عليه السلام وذريته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks first for himself because he wants his descendants to attain and join him in excellence, as in his request for lasting good mention and in God’s making him an imam and his descendants after a trial.
rows.anchor: وقد أفرد نفسه في جميع الفقرات الثلاث عن غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “My sons” in the first prayer and “my descendants” here both mean some descendants, so the two requests agree.
rows.anchor: فقد تقدم أن المراد ببنيه بعضهم لا جميعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking God to accept the prayer intensifies and insists on it, just as the explanation that idols led many astray reinforces the first request.
rows.anchor: فإن سؤال تقبل الدعاء إلحاح وإصرار وتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham closes his final prayer recorded in the Qur’an by asking forgiveness for himself, his parents, and believers on the Day of Reckoning, resembling Noah’s closing prayer.
rows.anchor: بطلب المغفرة للمؤمنين يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer for both parents in Abraham’s late-life prayer indicates that Azar was not his biological father: Abraham had already disavowed Azar after an earlier promised intercession, while later Qur’anic prayers show he prayed for his parents.
rows.anchor: لم يكن ولد آزر المشرك لصلبه فإنه عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated vocatives vary between “my Lord” and “our Lord”: requests specific to Abraham’s precedence and imamate use the singular, while shared requests use the plural.
rows.anchor: النداء المكرر الذي فيه بلفظ { رب } و { ربنا } والعناية فيما أضيف

words: رب اجعل هذا البلد آمنا واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام
rows.speaker: عقيل بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: A report in al-Durr al-Manthūr says the Prophet recited Abraham’s prayer from this sura to six men of the Ansar at al-ʿAqaba; they were moved and responded to his invitation.
rows.anchor: عن عقيل بن أبي طالب أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم لما أتاه الستة النفر

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-ʿAyyāshī transmits from Abū ʿUbayda that al-Ṣādiq said whoever loves the Imams is of the Ahl al-Bayt, citing Abraham’s “whoever follows me belongs to me.”
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن أبي عبيدة عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال من أحبنا فهو منا أهل البيت

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A second al-ʿAyyāshī report has al-Ṣādiq say that those among the audience who fear God and act righteously are of the Ahl al-Bayt; he and ʿUmar ibn Yazīd affirm their inclusion among Muḥammad’s family by reference to Abraham’s words and 3:68.
rows.anchor: وفيه عن محمد الحلبي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال من اتقى الله منكم وأصلح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls apparently reported claims that Ishmael’s descendants never worshipped idols after Abraham’s prayer, but merely treated them as intercessors, likely fabricated, in light of his preceding argument.
rows.anchor: أن الرواية موضوعة، وقد تقدمت الإشارة إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports that Taif was moved from Palestine to Mecca, circled the House seven times, then settled at its present site are possible as a miracle but weak and mursal, insufficient proof; such a great sign would have been mentioned in this passage of blessing.
rows.anchor: وهذا وإن كان ممكن الوقوع في نفسه من طريق الإعجاز لكن لا يكفي لثبوته أمثال هذه الروايات الضعيفة

rows.speaker: أحدهما عليهما السلام
rows.claim: A mursal al-ʿAyyāshī report from Ḥarīz, citing an unnamed Imam, gives a reading “for my two sons,” meaning Ishmael and Isaac; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the report is weak and should be disregarded.
rows.anchor: أنه كان يقرأ { رب اغفر لي ولولدي } يعني إسماعيل وإسحاق

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: A second mursal al-ʿAyyāshī report, from Jābir and Abū Jaʿfar, gives the same “my two sons” reading; the author regards both reports as weak and says they imply Abraham’s father was an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام مثله وظاهر هذه الرواية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning concerns an exterminating punishment that removes the unjust among a community; as in 10:103, only a group of wrongdoers is struck, not every individual.
rows.anchor: وإنما يصيب الأمة الظالمة بحلول أجلهم وهم طائفة من ظالمي الأمة لا جميع أفرادها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Extermination is a judgment between a messenger and those who reject the call, prescribed for communities including Muḥammad’s, and repeatedly threatened in the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم في تفسير سورة يونس وغيره أن ذلك مكتوب على الأمم قضاء بينهم وبين رسولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This day purges the earth of idolatry and injustice until only believers remain and all religion belongs to God; he connects it with the promise that righteous servants inherit the earth.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو اليوم الذي يطهر الله الأرض فيه من قذارة الشرك والظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that the preceding restriction confines punishment to Resurrection does not rule out a different worldly punishment; reading this warning as only Resurrection would override its context and the many verses predicting punishment for this community.
rows.anchor: ولا ينافي انحصاره في يوم القيامة وجود نوع آخر من العذاب في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are those overtaken by extermination; they ask for a short extension of earthly life to make up what their wrongdoing made them lose, as their promise to answer and follow shows.
rows.anchor: الاستمهال بمدة قصيرة تضاف إلى عمرهم في الدنيا حتى يتداركوا فيه ما فوتوه بظلمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say “the messengers” in the plural because the principle behind this punishment is judgment between every messenger and those who reject him, not a rule limited to one messenger.
rows.anchor: والتعبير بالرسل بلفظ الجمع في قولهم

words: أقسمتم من قبل ما لكم من زوال
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An oath stakes a claim on something honored to establish its truth and is among the strongest means of emphasis; here it may figuratively mean a categorical, unequivocal assertion.
rows.anchor: الإقسام تعليق الحكم في الكلام بأمر شريف من جهة شرافته

words: أولم تكونوا أقسمتم من قبل ما لكم من زوال
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied speaker rebukes them: they had confidently claimed their power and defenses made them a lasting, dominant community, so why now ask for more time?
rows.anchor: والمعنى يقال لهم توبيخا وتبكيتا ألم تكونوا أقسمتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about inhabiting the dwellings of former wrongdoers is coordinated with the preceding clause at the syntactic level of “you swore.”
rows.anchor: معطوف على محل قوله { أقسمتم } في الآية السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their stay in the earlier peoples’ homes should have shown the truth of the prophetic call in two ways: observing the wrongdoers’ fate and hearing parables and warnings of the destruction that follows rejection.
rows.anchor: جهة المشاهدة حيث تبين لكم كيف فعلنا بأولئك الظالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plotting clause is circumstantial, attached to the subject pronoun of “what We did,” to that of “against them,” or to both; its plural pronouns refer to the former wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: فيها أو من الضميرين جميعا على ما قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their plot is “with God” because His knowledge and power encompass it; plotting works only when its target is unaware and unable to thwart it, otherwise it fails or rebounds on the plotter.
rows.anchor: والمراد بكون مكرهم عند الله إحاطته تعالى به بعلمه وقدرته

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: On one account, in is concessive and the lām in “would move” attaches to an implied verb such as “require”: God encompasses their plotting even if it were mountain-moving in force.
rows.anchor: متعلق بمقدر يدل عليه لفظ المكر كقولنا يقتضي أو يوجب

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes in as negative and mountains as a metaphor for God’s firm signs and miracles, which their plot cannot undo; the author calls this reading remote.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالجبال الآيات والمعجزات كناية

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: The mountain-moving interpretation is supported by a reading attributed to Ibn Masʿūd, “وما كان مكرهم”; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī still judges the interpretation remote.
rows.anchor: وأيد هذا المعنى بقراءة ابن مسعود { وما كان مكرهم } وهو معنى بعيد

rows.speaker: قُرئ
rows.claim: A reading with fatḥa on the first lām and ḍamma on the second takes in as a light form of emphatic inna: their plot was so immense that mountains would move.
rows.anchor: بفتح اللام الأولى وضم اللام الثانية

words: فلا تحسبن الله مخلف وعده رسله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command follows from the delayed punishment: God will not fail His messengers’ promise of support and of taking wrongdoers to account.
rows.anchor: تفريع على ما تقدم أن ترك مؤاخذة الظالمين بعملهم إنما هو لتأخيرهم إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God cannot fail through incapacity or a later overpowering change, because He is absolutely mighty, capable, and never overcome.
rows.anchor: فإن إخلاف الوعد إما لكون الواعد غير قادر على إنجاز ما وعده أو لتغير من الرأي بعروض حال ثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine retribution vindicates truth against the arrogant and gives the oppressed justice against oppressors; the name “Possessor of Retribution” is paired in Qur’anic usage with “Mighty.”
rows.anchor: وذو انتقام من أسمائه تعالى الحسنى التي سمى الله تعالى بها نفسه في مواضع من كلامه وقارنه في جميعها باسمه العزيز
